title: TypeScript Advanced Patterns
description: Level up your TypeScript — utility types, generics, type guards, mapped types, and common patterns.

entries.label: Partial & Required
entries.command:
type UpdateUser = Partial<User>      // all fields optional
type FullUser = Required<User>       // all fields required
entries.description: Make all properties optional or required — essential for update DTOs

entries.label: Pick & Omit
entries.command:
type UserPreview = Pick<User, 'id' | 'name' | 'avatar'>
type UserCreate = Omit<User, 'id' | 'createdAt'>
entries.description: Create subset types by including or excluding specific properties

entries.label: Record Type
entries.description: Create an object type with known keys and a consistent value type

entries.label: Discriminated Union
entries.description: Pattern matching with tagged unions — TypeScript narrows automatically

entries.label: Type Guard
entries.description: Custom type guard function — narrows types in if/switch blocks

entries.label: Generic Function
entries.description: Write reusable functions that preserve input types

entries.label: Generic Constraint
entries.description: Constrain generics to ensure type safety — K must be a key of T

entries.label: Const Assertion
entries.command:
const ROLES = ['admin', 'editor', 'viewer'] as const
type Role = typeof ROLES[number]  // 'admin' | 'editor' | 'viewer'
entries.description: Derive literal union types from arrays — no duplication, always in sync

entries.label: Satisfies Operator
entries.description: Validate a value matches a type without widening it

entries.label: Zod Schema Inference
entries.description: Derive TypeScript types from Zod schemas — single source of truth
